openings.claim: Rim-anchored side stops with loose vertical capture might register the hatch without increasing seal compression.
openings.delta: Change the lateral carrier from hatch friction to bearing against two M4 stop bolts. Use four bolts to anchor two padded strip pairs to the rim alone, and the remaining two as side stops near opposing hatch edges. Upper strips overlap the hatch with slight vertical clearance. Withdraw both assemblies fully for inspection, retaining assemblies and pads with cord. Drill and cut only supplied strips.
openings.prediction: Against G0049:R1's pressure-clamp rival, registration could persist with little hatch compression: the hatch approaches a stop, movement stays within 1 mm, and marked anchors remain stationary. This predicts lateral bearing without reproducing the observed opposite-corner lift. Friction clamps could also pass; outcome success alone would not distinguish them. Final card disturbance must still permit retention and timely reopening.
openings.probe: First establish whether the unspecified rim permits separate anchoring, bolt-to-edge contact and vertical capture with the available strips; reject if not. Fabricate within ninety minutes. Run ten numbered closure/pull cycles within twenty observation minutes, with the final right-contact card disturbance. Record hatch and anchor displacement, visible stop contact, corner lift, reopening time and seal tears. Check the full aperture after withdrawing assemblies. Stationary anchors plus movement arrested at stop contact supports the proposed load path; anchor slip, absent contact or pressure-dependent retention defeats it. Reject on permanent deformation, new seal tears, unrecoverable components or any outcome failure.
assumptions: Rim profile, hatch edge access and bolt clearance permit this geometry without fixture alteration; these indispensable dimensions are unknown.
Pads can protect rim anchoring, and strips, bolts and anchors can carry 20 N without bending or slipping; capacity is unproved.
Two stops sufficiently constrain the supplied pull direction and repeated placement; otherwise registration fails.
Vertical clearance accommodates the final 1 mm card while preventing escape; available cord permits recovery outside the opening within 30 seconds.

assessment: One geometry-and-capacity probe, not deployment. Positive lateral bearing transfers the compression problem to rim anchoring and stop geometry; feasibility remains uncertain.

lineage.reason: Separate lateral registration from hatch compression while retaining removable padded strip assemblies and explicit geometry/resource limits.
